oft_parallel_action_decoding.Why does autoregressive OpenVLA need K *: Count tokens per action and per chunk under next-token decoding with a causal mask, then say what changes in the inputs (empty slots) and in the mask so every slot is predicted from the same pass.

oft_parallel_action_decoding.Walk through the multimodal sequence OFT: Lay out the indices: patches spliced after BOS, prompt ending in 29871, N slots, then </s>. Locate the first slot and explain the one-left offset shared with training.
oft_parallel_action_decoding.OFT's patched attention copies the last: Ask what the last query is allowed to see under a causal mask, then add padding. Contrast who attends to the action slots in full bidirectional attention versus a prefix-LM.

oft_parallel_action_decoding.Parallel L1 decoding in one pass versus: Weigh passes per chunk and chunk execution time against expressiveness for multimodal demos; mention what the OFT paper found for L1 versus diffusion on its tasks.

latent_action_quantizer.What is a latent action, and how do LAPA: Cover the encoder as an inverse-dynamics model over a frame pair, the decoder as a world model, the code index as a pseudo-label the VLM predicts, and the later swap to a real action head on labelled data.
latent_action_quantizer.Why does a VQ-VAE need a special trick t: Start from argmin having no useful derivative. Explain what x + stop_grad(q - x) evaluates to in the forward pass and what its gradient is in the backward pass, and what it leaves untrained.
latent_action_quantizer.In straight-through VQ, which parameters: Trace where stop_grad sits in each term. Discuss codes that never move without the codebook term, and an encoder whose outputs drift away from the codes without commitment; mention the role of beta.
latent_action_quantizer.Write the NSVQ substitution and explain: Write the replacement of q - x by a scaled random direction, then follow the gradient through the residual norm back to the chosen code. Compare the forward distance to the true quantization error.
latent_action_quantizer.How do you detect and repair dead codes,: Cover usage counting over a window, a threshold on the usage rate, copying live codes with a small perturbation, and when to stop. Relate exp(entropy) of usage to the effective number of codes.
latent_action_quantizer.Quantizing the difference of frame featu: Contrast a code driven by change alone with one that can also encode scene appearance. Discuss camera motion and distractors, and how UniVLA's language-conditioned stage tries to separate task-relevant dynamics.
latent_action_quantizer.Discrete latent action codes versus GR00: Compare a token head with cross-entropy over a small vocabulary to regressing a continuous vector. Discuss information lost by quantization, compatibility with VLM token heads, and multimodality.

knowledge_insulation_attention.What problem does knowledge insulation s: Start from gradient interference: a random expert's flow loss flowing into pre-trained weights. Then cover what the backbone loses if it gets no action loss at all, and what the FAST next-token loss gives it instead.
knowledge_insulation_attention.In a KI-trained pi0.5, which token group: Go group by group: what the prefix sees, the causal rule inside FAST, what the expert tokens see. Then name the two pairs that are blocked and why the VLM never reads the expert.
knowledge_insulation_attention.Where exactly does the stop-gradient go: Locate it on the expert-query path: which of Q, K, V, and for which token positions. Then explain why detach changes only the backward graph, so values and inference stay the same.
knowledge_insulation_attention.Why must the action-expert tokens be blo: Think about what the FAST tokens encode for the very chunk being denoised. Then trace the cumulative att_masks rule: which earlier blocks a later block can see, and so why an explicit block is needed.
knowledge_insulation_attention.With FAST tokens in the training sequenc: Compare the sequence the expert sees in training with the one at inference. Cover how RoPE positions are counted, where the actions start in each case, and what a shifted offset does to learned attention.
knowledge_insulation_attention.Knowledge insulation versus freezing the: Compare three settings: freezing, joint training without a stop-gradient, and KI. For each, say what is trained by which loss and how it affects language following, action quality and convergence speed.
knowledge_insulation_attention.KI's mask forbids attention in both dire: Contrast the two leak directions: autoregressive tokens reading continuous inputs, and the expert reading FAST tokens. Cover what each makes easy to learn, what happens at inference, and the paper's ablation evidence.

recap_advantage_conditioning.What does the improvement indicator in R: Start from I = 1[A > eps] and apply Bayes rule to p(I | A). Cover what pi(a | I, o) equals at beta = 1 in Eq. 2, and why every example still gets a supervised label.
recap_advantage_conditioning.Why does RECAP define the reward as -1 p: Sum the rewards from t to the end for a success and for a failure. Cover what the value counts, the per-task normalization by maximum episode length, and why one sparse success label is enough.

recap_advantage_conditioning.The pi*0.6 paper describes the advantage: Compare the 30th and 70th percentiles and the positive share each gives. Cover grouping by task, the quantile rule, strict comparison at ties, and the fractions the appendix uses in pre-training and fine-tuning.
recap_advantage_conditioning.Why does RECAP drop the advantage indica: Think about which two policies one network must represent. Cover what dropout replaces in Eq. 3, the Eq. 13 combination, and what beta = 1 reduces to.
recap_advantage_conditioning.Advantage conditioning versus advantage-: Compare what each needs from the model: a likelihood, a weight per example, or a label per example. Cover what happens to low-advantage data in each and why flow matching makes policy gradients awkward.
recap_advantage_conditioning.Raising the positive fraction versus rai: Contrast sharpening at training time with sharpening at inference. Cover how a smaller positive share selects better actions, and what large CFG weights do to the action distribution's support.

fsq_quantizer.FSQ versus VQ for a video tokenizer that: Weigh codebook usage and training stability, codebook parameters and encoder output width, and what a learned codebook can model that an axis-aligned grid cannot.
fsq_quantizer.How would you choose the levels for a ta: Discuss products of levels that approximate a power of two, the paper's Table 1 and its heuristic of at least 5 levels per channel, and the trade between channel count and resolution per channel.

diffusion_forcing_schedule.How does Diffusion Forcing's training di: Contrast what the model is conditioned on in each regime: clean history, one shared level, or an independent level per frame. Then say why training on every mix of levels lets one network run several sampling schedules.

self_forcing_rollout.Count the denoise calls, cache calls and: Per block: denoise calls before and at the exit, one cache call, one randn per re-noise plus one for the cache. Then repeat for inference, where every block runs all 4 steps.
